questions.q: A team needs to copy rows from a database into Kafka and later from Kafka into a search index, without writing producer or consumer code. What does Kafka provide for this?

options.t: Kafka Streams, with a database client inside each processor
options.why: Streams processes data already in Kafka; moving data in and out is Connect's job.

options.t: Kafka Connect: a source connector in, a sink connector out
MirrorMaker 2, pointed at the database
options.why: MirrorMaker 2 copies between Kafka clusters.

options.t: The Admin API's import and export methods
options.why: The Admin API manages topics and configs; it doesn't copy data.

questions.explain: Kafka Connect streams data between Kafka and other systems: source connectors import into Kafka, sink connectors export from it.

questions.q: Which kind of connector writes data from Kafka topics into an external system?

options.t: A source connector
options.why: Source connectors import into Kafka.

options.t: A converter
options.why: Converters change data formats; they aren't connectors.

options.t: A sink connector
A single message transform
options.why: SMTs change records; they don't move data.

questions.explain: Source connectors import data into Kafka; sink connectors export data from Kafka to other systems.

questions.q: What does distributed mode give that standalone mode doesn't?

options.t: A REST API for managing connectors, which standalone mode lacks
options.why: The REST API is available in both modes.

options.t: Support for source connectors
options.why: Both modes run source and sink connectors.

options.t: The ability to use converters
options.why: Converters work in both modes.

options.t: Fault tolerance, with work shared across workers

questions.explain: Standalone is one process with no fault tolerance. Distributed mode balances work across workers, scales, and is fault tolerant for tasks, configuration and offsets.

questions.q: How are connectors created on a distributed Connect cluster?

options.t: Through the REST API
By passing properties files on the worker's command line
options.why: That is standalone mode; distributed mode doesn't take connector configs on the command line.

options.t: By writing them into the config topic by hand
options.why: Workers manage the config topic themselves.

options.t: With kafka-configs --entity-type connectors
options.why: No such entity type exists.

questions.explain: In distributed mode connector configurations aren't passed on the command line: the REST API creates, modifies and deletes connectors.

questions.q: Distributed workers keep their state in three internal topics. Which one must have exactly one partition?

options.t: offset.storage.topic
options.why: The offsets topic is meant to have many partitions.

options.t: status.storage.topic
options.why: The status topic has no single-partition rule.

options.t: config.storage.topic
None; all three need many partitions
options.why: The config topic needs one partition.

questions.explain: `config.storage.topic` has one partition (replicated, compacted); `offset.storage.topic` has many partitions; all three are replicated and compacted.

questions.q: What does a connector instance do, compared with its tasks?

options.t: The connector copies the data; tasks only report status
options.why: It's the reverse: tasks copy, the connector plans.

options.t: The connector splits the job into tasks; tasks copy the data
Connectors and tasks are simply two names for the very same thing
options.why: They have different roles.

options.t: Each task runs a separate connector of its own
options.why: Tasks belong to one connector.

questions.explain: A connector does no copying itself: its configuration describes the data, and it breaks the job into tasks, which workers run to copy data.

questions.q: A connector is configured with `tasks.max=10` but only ever runs 4 tasks. Why might that be correct?

options.t: tasks.max is a maximum; a connector may create fewer tasks
Only 4 workers exist, and tasks are limited to one per worker
options.why: Workers can run several tasks each.

options.t: tasks.max is ignored in distributed mode
options.why: It applies in both modes.

options.t: Kafka Connect caps tasks at 4 per connector by default
options.why: There's no such cap; the connector decides up to tasks.max.

questions.explain: `tasks.max` is the maximum number of tasks; a connector may create fewer if it can't reach that parallelism.

questions.q: A file source connector restarts. How does it know which lines it has already sent?

options.t: It re-reads its output topic to find the last line it wrote there before
options.why: Source offsets are stored by Connect; it doesn't scan the topic.

options.t: It starts over from the start of the file every time
options.why: Connect's offset management lets it resume.

options.t: The broker remembers each source file's position
options.why: Connect stores source offsets, not the broker on its own.

options.t: Each record carries a source partition and offset that Connect stores

questions.explain: A source task emits `SourceRecord`s with a source partition (the file) and source offset (the byte position). Connect stores these offsets, so the task resumes where it stopped.

questions.q: What do `key.converter` and `value.converter` control?

options.t: Which tables or files a connector reads
options.why: That's connector-specific configuration.

options.t: How records are transformed one by one
options.why: That's what single message transforms do.

options.t: How Connect data is serialized into the bytes written to Kafka
Which brokers a worker connects to
options.why: That's bootstrap.servers.

questions.explain: Converters translate between Kafka Connect's data format and the serialized bytes in Kafka. They are independent of connectors, so any connector works with any format.

questions.q: Workers use a JSON converter, but one connector must write Avro. What is the cleanest way?

options.t: Run a separate Connect cluster just for that one Avro connector
options.why: Converters can be overridden per connector.

options.t: Override key.converter / value.converter in its own config
Use an SMT to turn the JSON into Avro bytes
options.why: Formats are the converter's job, and it can be set per connector.

options.t: Change the topic's compression.type to avro
options.why: Avro isn't a compression type.

questions.explain: Converters are set on the worker and can be overridden per connector with `key.converter` and `value.converter` in the connector's configuration.

questions.q: A sink connector reading plain JSON objects fails because the JSON converter expects a schema-and-payload envelope. Which setting writes and reads schemaless JSON?

options.t: value.converter.schemas.enable=false
errors.tolerance=all
options.why: That would skip records, not read them.

options.t: value.converter=none
options.why: There is no 'none' converter.

options.t: schemas.registry=off on the worker
options.why: No such setting exists.

questions.explain: With the JSON converter, setting `key.converter.schemas.enable` / `value.converter.schemas.enable` to false gives schemaless JSON.

questions.q: What is a single message transform (SMT)?

options.t: A Kafka Streams operator used inside connectors
options.why: SMTs are part of Connect, not Streams.

options.t: A converter for one record type
options.why: Converters handle serialization.

options.t: A broker plugin that rewrites records after they are stored
options.why: SMTs run in Connect; brokers never rewrite records.

options.t: A light, one-record-at-a-time change applied in Connect

questions.explain: SMTs make lightweight changes to one record at a time, chained with `transforms`. Built-ins include `InsertField`, `MaskField`, `Filter` and `Cast`.

questions.q: Before a sink writes customer records, a field `card_number` must be hidden. Which built-in SMT is meant for that?

options.t: Flatten
options.why: Flatten turns nested structures into flat ones.

options.t: MaskField
HoistField
options.why: HoistField wraps data inside a field.

options.t: InsertHeader
options.why: InsertHeader adds a header.

questions.explain: `MaskField` replaces a field's value; other built-ins include `InsertField`, `Flatten`, `HoistField`, `Cast` and `Filter`.

questions.q: A connector must drop test records (those with a header `env=test`) and pass the rest unchanged. Which combination does that?

options.t: The Filter transform, with a predicate matching those records
errors.tolerance=all, so the test records fail and are skipped
options.why: That skips records that fail, and hides real errors too.

options.t: A converter that rejects records with that header
options.why: Converters serialize; selecting records is for transforms and predicates.

options.t: MaskField on every field of the test records
options.why: Masking keeps the records; it doesn't drop them.

questions.explain: Transformations can be applied conditionally with predicates; combined with `Filter`, predicates drop selected messages.

questions.q: With default settings, what does a connector do when one record fails conversion?

options.t: It skips the record and logs it
options.why: Skipping needs errors.tolerance=all; logging needs errors.log.enable=true.

options.t: It sends the record to a dead-letter topic
options.why: A dead-letter topic must be configured.

options.t: It fails fast: the task stops
It retries the record forever
options.why: errors.retry.timeout defaults to 0: no retries.

questions.explain: By default a connector fails fast on a conversion or transform error: `errors.tolerance=none`, `errors.retry.timeout=0`, `errors.log.enable=false`.

questions.q: Which TWO settings make a sink connector keep running past bad records while keeping them for inspection?

options.t: errors.tolerance=all
errors.retry.timeout=0
options.why: That's the default and turns retries off; it doesn't keep bad records.

options.t: errors.deadletterqueue.topic.name=<topic>
tasks.max=1
options.why: Task count doesn't affect error handling.

options.t: offset.flush.interval.ms=0
options.why: This isn't an error-handling setting.

questions.explain: `errors.tolerance=all` skips bad records; `errors.deadletterqueue.topic.name` sends them, for a sink connector, to a dead-letter topic.

questions.q: Records reach a sink's dead-letter topic, but nobody can tell why each failed. Which setting adds the error context to them?

options.t: errors.log.include.messages=true, set on the brokers instead
options.why: Connect error settings belong to the connector, not the broker.

options.t: errors.tolerance=none
options.why: That stops the connector at the first error.

options.t: errors.deadletterqueue.context.headers.enable=true
value.converter.schemas.enable=true
options.why: This changes JSON format, not error context.

questions.explain: `errors.deadletterqueue.context.headers.enable=true` adds the error context to dead-letter records as headers.

questions.q: Which kind of connector can send failed records to a dead-letter topic with Connect's built-in error handling?

options.t: Source connectors only
options.why: The dead-letter queue setting applies to sink connectors.

options.t: Both, in the same way
options.why: The docs describe it for sink connectors.

options.t: Neither; it needs a custom SMT
options.why: It is built in, for sinks.

options.t: Sink connectors

questions.explain: `errors.deadletterqueue.topic.name` sends failed records to a dead-letter topic for a sink connector.

questions.q: What is needed for exactly-once delivery from a source connector?

options.t: exactly.once.source.support=enabled on all workers, plus connector support
processing.guarantee=exactly_once_v2 on the connector
options.why: That's a Kafka Streams setting.

options.t: isolation.level=read_committed on the worker
options.why: That's for consumers reading transactional data.

options.t: Nothing extra: every source connector is exactly-once once workers run 4.x
options.why: It must be enabled, and the connector must support it.

questions.explain: Exactly-once source connectors need `exactly.once.source.support=enabled` on every worker (existing clusters need two rolling upgrades), and the connector must support it.

questions.q: A distributed Connect cluster is given `group.id=orders-app`, which a consumer application already uses. Why is that a problem?

options.t: Group IDs must start with connect-
options.why: There's no such naming rule.

options.t: Connect's group.id must not conflict with consumer group IDs
Distributed workers can't have a group.id
options.why: They need one to form the cluster.

options.t: It is only a problem in standalone mode, where workers share one group
options.why: group.id forms the distributed cluster.

questions.explain: Distributed workers share a `group.id` to form the Connect cluster, and the docs say it must not conflict with consumer group IDs.

questions.q: On a secured cluster, a worker connects fine but its sink tasks' consumers can't authenticate. Why?

options.t: Sink tasks always connect anonymously
options.why: They use the security settings they are given.

options.t: The worker must be restarted after each connector
options.why: That doesn't fix missing settings.

options.t: The ACLs only allow the worker's own internal topics, not the sink's
options.why: The failure here is authentication, which needs credentials.

options.t: Their settings need the consumer. prefix on the worker

questions.explain: Worker settings without a prefix are for Connect's own topics. Sink tasks' consumers take `consumer.`-prefixed settings, source tasks' producers `producer.`-prefixed ones; only `bootstrap.servers` is inherited, so a secured cluster needs the settings up to three times.

questions.q: One sink connector should read with `max.poll.records=100`, while others keep the worker default. Where is this set?

options.t: consumer.override.max.poll.records=100 in that connector's config
max.poll.records=100 in that connector's config
options.why: Client overrides per connector take the consumer.override. prefix.

options.t: consumer.max.poll.records=100, set in the worker's own properties file
options.why: That changes every sink connector on the worker.

options.t: It can't be set per connector
options.why: Per-connector overrides exist.

questions.explain: Client settings can be overridden per connector with `producer.override.` (sources) and `consumer.override.` (sinks).

questions.q: Which consumer group does a sink connector named `es-orders` use by default?

options.t: es-orders
options.why: Connect adds a prefix.

options.t: The worker's group.id
options.why: That forms the Connect cluster; sinks get their own groups.

options.t: connect-es-orders
A random group on each start

questions.explain: A sink connector's consumer group is `connect-<connector name>` by default (or a group ID set by override).
